ui.note: Document neutral sign-up followed by explicit sign-in, including email-bound invitation and pending native approval journeys in all six locales. Document local timer persistence and the reload limit: a forward device-clock correction can credit unworked time up to the interval length. Start and resume now anchor elapsed time at the action. Completion replay, dismissible logging errors, server permissions, timestamp validation and persisted formats remain unchanged. Import completion and conflict transfer focus during the DOM commit; moving focus during a status retry cancels the handoff, which also rechecks focus before committing. Import inputs, acknowledgment and persistence are unchanged. Document the browser connection requirement on opening or reloading, automatic and manual retries for transport failures, and continued offline editing in already-open tabs. HTTP session and startup refusals keep their existing behavior; no cached identity or offline startup is added. Once the session has resolved, a signed-out refetch after a sign-up or sign-in attempt no longer remounts Login, while the first fetch keeps the boot skeleton, so the entered email, the sign-up notice and sign-in errors stay visible; no documented flow changes.

release.note: Prepare the first beta, 0.1.0-beta.1 with Android code 13, retain the existing signing certificate and documentation epoch, align release commands, and describe the remaining prerelease and native qualification limits. Generated publication notes now describe a prerelease rather than an alpha.

configuration.note: Align the default app and Zero image pair with beta.1 in the packaged guides. This release changes image versions, not operator settings or the retained credentials required for upgrades.

deployment.note: Align chart metadata, resource labels and packaged deployment image examples with 0.1.0-beta.1. Preserve app/Zero pairing, storage and recovery guidance, and cluster qualification limits; the optional one-image bundle remains separate from standard release assets.

native.note: Document the branch-scoped hosted desktop journey harness, ephemeral trusted HTTPS fixture, per-journey evidence and platform limits. macOS evaluation is debug-only and requires explicit test configuration; optimized release binaries must exclude it. Sign-out now starts retired notification cleanup after durable local revocation. Normal close settles pending sync handshakes within their existing deadline before cancellation, preserving offline evidence after network failure while retaining trust and interruption refusals. Client protocols, stored formats, backups, upgrade and rollback procedures are unchanged. Windows/macOS notifications remain unsupported and are not credited as passing journeys. The handshake regression uses an explicit setup barrier without changing runtime behavior. Debug builds record native transport error causes for runner diagnosis; release error handling and trust rules are unchanged.

authentication.note: OAuth registration denials preserve their stable policy code through Better Auth callback redirects. Native browser sign-in retains the grant ID and displays the localized policy message. Document periodic stream revalidation after session revocation; HTTP authorization remains checked against live session state. Invitations remain HTTPS browser links with fragment tokens and backward-compatible acceptance; native task scheme handling is unchanged. Document the current account name, identity update validation, synced display behavior, and managed-account normalization with JSON validation errors. Production startup validates secret length and retained JWKS decryption. The authentication guide links the stopped-replica secret rotation procedure instead of direct replacement. Browser sign-in checks the per-IP ceiling before creating IP-plus-email buckets. The handoff and trusted-proxy guides document that order, unchanged limits and batch-drained cleanup; docs/security.md records the body bound and unchanged TOTP lockout. The authentication guides already changed in this branch document neutral public email sign-up, explicit sign-in without SMTP, admission policy and unchanged native approval. This follow-up preserves that public and native protocol: only identity and password fields reach account creation, and persistence failures use the existing neutral result and timing floor. docs/security.md now describes discarded fields and operator-visible failure logs. No new setup, recovery, native trust, account admission, or credential storage procedure is introduced; managed-account creation retains explicit failures. Unexpected registration-policy failures are logged and return a generic unavailable error instead of a policy refusal carrying the raw message; documented refusals are unchanged.

compatibility.note: Document restricted-role membership removal without TEMP and uniform 404 attachment denials, with unchanged persisted formats. Attachment garbage collection uses the same checked-out connection as its leader lock. Persisted attachment states, ciphertext format, quotas and restore procedures are unchanged. The storage startup probe and sanitized upload diagnostics do not change persisted attachment formats; restore guidance now covers directory permissions and matching authentication secrets. Add restricted notification cleanup policies and triggers for self-service leave under every runtime membership role. Browser startup fetches distinguish transport rejection from received HTTP responses. No auth evidence, synced data, storage keys or persisted formats are added or changed. The desktop guide documents the bounded credential records and journal that #1090 adds.
compatibility.upgrade: Deploy the application update without schema, blob or key conversion; runtime TEMP grants are unnecessary. No schema or ciphertext migration is required; restart the application with the updated image. Before upgrading, provision the filesystem directory when attachments are enabled and retain the existing authentication secret. Run the additive membership-leave migration before deploying the application that exposes Leave workspace.
compatibility.backup: Keep the existing coordinated database and blob backups; ciphertext and key envelopes are unchanged. The existing database and attachment backup procedure remains applicable without changes. Back up the database, attachment ciphertext, field keys, and authentication secret as a matching recovery set. Keep coordinated database and attachment backups; existing rows, ciphertext and key envelopes are unchanged. Desktop credential records live in the OS credential store and are not part of server backups; sign in online again after a server restore.
compatibility.rollback: The previous application remains data-compatible but restores the TEMP dependency and foreign attachment 403 response. The prior application can use the same database and attachment objects; no format changes occur. Restore matching database and secret backups or reverse authentication-secret rotation while all replicas are stopped. The previous application can retain the additive migration; do not overwrite newer membership changes with an older database. Older desktop builds cannot read the bounded credential records: sign out and remove native session records before a desktop rollback.
compatibility.clientVersions: Existing web, Android and desktop clients use unchanged attachment formats and interpret unauthorized downloads as unavailable. Browser, Android and desktop clients use the same attachment protocol and remain compatible. Browser and native clients remain compatible; attachment formats, quotas, permissions, and transfer payloads are unchanged. Existing clients continue to work; updated clients expose Leave workspace and the server enforces the same cleanup for every role. Desktop stored sessions in the earlier evidence format need one online start to populate offline evidence.

clients.note: Document the retained runtime notice manifest, exact source URLs and SHA-256 checksums, extracted-archive integrity qualification, and unchanged incomplete runtime license coverage and binary publication block.
